prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The best parent (c011/c018 lineage) already clamps momentum decay to 0.5 and caps per-net weight; the remaining TNS lever inside `update_net_weights` is the *degree threshold* used to ignore high-fanout nets — lowering the effective `ignore_net_degree` cap so that moderate-fanout nets (which carry many moderate violations) also receive timing weight, while still skipping true clock/reset high-fanout nets, should spread repair effort and reduce TNS broadly.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.947 robust(mean-std)=+0.278 min_case=+0.274 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.365 dWNS=+24.9% dTNS=+44.5% overflow~135
  bp-ng45: score=+0.308 dWNS=+24.2% dTNS=+35.4% overflow~131
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.274 dWNS=+25.6% dTNS=+28.4% overflow~120
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains (+28–45%) exceeding dWNS (+24–26%), consistent with spreading repair to moderate-fanout nets. bp-ng45 and ariane133-ng45 moved most; bp_fe-ng45 least, plausibly because its violation mix is dominated by true high-fanout nets still skipped. Overflow ~120–135 is stable, so no legality concern. Next step: sweep the effective `ignore_net_degree` cap (e.g., 200/150/100) to find where moderate-fanout weighting saturates before clock/reset nets leak in, and confirm TNS gains persist without overflow regression.
